content.text:
All 9 tests pass. `node --test`: `# pass 9`, `# fail 0`.

**What was wrong in `duration.js`** (only file changed — `duration.test.js` untouched, confirmed via `git status`):

1. `parseDuration` used an unanchored global regex (`/(\d+)([dhms])/g`) in a `exec` loop, so it silently summed whatever fragments it found and ignored everything else. That accepted empty input, stray characters (`1hxx30m`), repeated units (`1h2h`), and out-of-order units (`30m1h`) — all of which must throw `RangeError`.
2. `formatDuration` joined an empty parts array for zero, returning `''` instead of the canonical `0s`.

**Fix:**
- An anchored shape check `/^\d+[dhms](?:\d+[dhms])*$/` rejects empty input, stray characters, and non-integer/negative/unitless forms up front with `RangeError`.
- A rank cursor over `Object.keys(UNITS)` (`d, h, m, s`) rejects any unit that repeats or appears after a smaller one.
- `formatDuration` returns `'0s'` when no unit contributes a nonzero part.
- `UNIT_ORDER` is derived from `UNITS`, so parse order and format order can't drift apart.

**Verification beyond the test file** — probed spec-derived cases directly: `''`, `' '`, `'1hxx30m'`, `'1h2h'`, `'30m1h'`, `'1s1m'`, `'1d1d'`, `'d'`, `'1'`, `'1x'`, `'-1h'`, `'1.5h'`, `'1h '`, `' 1h'`, `'1H'`, and non-string inputs all throw `RangeError`; `'0s'`, `'1s'`, `'1m'`, `'1h'`, `'1d'`, `'2d4h5m6s'`, `'1d1h1m1s'` parse and round-trip exactly.

One behavior the spec doesn't pin down: `formatDuration` truncates sub-second remainders, so `formatDuration(999) === '0s'`. Since the units stop at `s`, I left truncation as-is rather than inventing rounding rules; say the word if you want it to throw or round instead.
